claims: The four major championships are The Masters, PGA Championship, U.S. Open, and The Open Championship.
A Grand Slam in golf signifies winning all four major championships either in a single calendar year or over a career.
Gene Sarazen, Ben Hogan, Gary Player, Jack Nicklaus, Tiger Woods, and Rory McIlroy.
The Calendar Grand Slam has never been done in the modern era.
Bobby Jones accomplished the Calendar Grand Slam in 1930.
The four majors in 1930 included the U.S. Open, Open Championship, U.S. Amateur, and British Amateur.
Tiger Woods held all four major titles simultaneously from 2000 to 2001.
Tiger Woods did not win all four major titles in a single calendar year.
Currently, no active male golfer holds all four major championships.
The Masters Tournament is held at Augusta National.
The Masters Tournament is held in early April.
The PGA Championship is run by the PGA of America.
The PGA Championship is usually held in May.
The U.S. Open is organized by the USGA.
The U.S. Open is held in mid-June.
The Open Championship is organized by the R&A.
The Open Championship is held in mid-July.
The LPGA defines the Grand Slam differently due to changing major lineups.
The Chevron Championship, U.S. Women's Open, KPMG Women's PGA Championship, Evian Championship, and AIG Women's Open.
The LPGA awards a Career Grand Slam for winning four of these distinct tournaments.
